theory.overview: A Trie, also called a prefix tree or digital tree, is a tree data structure used for efficient retrieval of a key in a dataset of strings. Unlike binary search trees, no node in the trie stores the key associated with that node; instead, its position in the tree defines the key. All descendants of a node have a common prefix of the string associated with that node. Tries enable O(m) lookups where m is key length, making them ideal for autocomplete, spell checking, and IP routing.

keyConcepts.name: Node Structure
keyConcepts.description: Each node has children (array or hash map) and a flag indicating if it's the end of a word. No single node stores the entire key.

keyConcepts.name: Prefix Search
keyConcepts.description: All descendants of a node share the prefix defined by the path to that node. Enables efficient prefix-based queries.

keyConcepts.name: Space Optimization
keyConcepts.description: Compressed Trie (Radix Tree) merges nodes with single children. Saves space for sparse datasets.

keyConcepts.name: Applications
keyConcepts.description: Autocomplete, spell checking, IP routing (longest prefix match), predictive text, and dictionary implementations.

algorithmSteps.description: Initialize empty trie with root node
Insert 'cat': Create path c→a→t, mark 't' as word end
Insert 'car': Reuse c→a, add new branch r, mark 'r' as end
Insert 'card': Extend from existing 'car' with new node d
Search 'car': Traverse c→a→r, node exists and isEnd=true. Found!
Prefix search 'ca': Returns all words with prefix 'ca'
